title: Reel: Indy metro has 21.3% more homes for sale, what that means for winter buyers
hook: If your home search stalled last winter because nothing fit, this winter looks different.
body: If your home search stalled last winter because nothing fit, this winter looks different. In October, 7,171 homes were for sale across the Indy metro. That's 21.3% more than a year earlier. For you, more listings means more room to compare and less need to rush. You can see a home twice, ask questions about the price, and walk away from one that doesn't fit. It also means a plan matters, because more homes take more sorting. We can narrow the field in Fishers, Carmel or Noblesville to the homes that match your budget and your commute. Call 317-863-9011 and ask for a winter home short list.

title: Reel: Buying in Fishers from out of state, what to ask a relocation agent
hook: How do you buy a home in Fishers when you still live in another state?
body: How do you buy a home in Fishers when you still live in another state? Start with the agent you hire, and ask a few direct questions. How will you help me compare Fishers with Carmel, Noblesville and Westfield, from commutes to property taxes? How will I see homes before I can fly in? Listen for live video tours and quick replies. And who keeps inspections, the appraisal and closing on track while I'm still packing? Clear answers tell you a lot. Vague answers tell you more. Call 317-863-9011 and book a 15-minute video call comparing Fishers, Carmel and Westfield.

body: What should you list your Fishers or Carmel home for this winter? Start here. Hamilton County's median list price was $445,000 in October, down 6.3% from a year earlier. Buyers also have more homes to compare than they did last fall, so they notice fast when a price was set from last spring's headlines. A price built from today's comparable homes, on your street and in your home's condition, gives buyers a reason to book the showing. One note: these are asking prices, not what homes closed for. title: Reel: Are prices going up or down in your town? Reading Noblesville headlines
hook: One Noblesville headline says prices are down, another says they're up, and both can be right.
body: One Noblesville headline says prices are down, another says they're up, and both can be right. Here's how to read them. First, is it a list price or a closed price? What sellers ask and what buyers actually paid can move in different directions. Next, what's the time frame? One month can swing, so compare it with the same month last year. Then, what's being measured? If more smaller homes sold in Noblesville, the median can dip while price per square foot climbs. That's how one town gets two headlines. Your street matters more than either. Text your street name to 317-863-9011 and ask for a local price check.

title: Reel: Building a new home in 2027? Why winter is when builder conversations start
hook: Want to move into a newly built home in 2027?
body: Want to move into a newly built home in 2027? The first conversations usually happen this winter, while model homes are quieter and you get more time with your questions. Across Westfield, Noblesville, Fishers and McCordsville, communities differ in lot sizes, build timelines and what's included versus an upgrade. Two things to know before your first visit. The builder's sales rep represents the builder. And ask about the agent registration policy, since some builders want your agent named at that first visit. On our team, Derek Evelo is the new construction specialist. Call 317-863-9011 and ask Derek for a side-by-side of the new-build communities on your list.

title: Reel: 2026 wrap, more homes for sale but fewer going under contract in Indy
hook: More homes were for sale around Indy this fall, yet fewer went under contract.
body: More homes were for sale around Indy this fall, yet fewer went under contract. In October, pending listings across the metro were down 12% from a year earlier. That's 2026 in one line. Buyers had more choices and took their time, and higher mortgage rates kept many of them careful. Heading into 2027, that cuts both ways. Sellers in Fishers, Carmel and Westfield need a price and a presentation that work from day one. Buyers have room to compare and negotiate. Either way, a plan beats a guess.
